HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The same shot. Queen Jinduk, a mild woman in her forties, sits very still and does not fidget as the crown, padded at the temples, comes down. The spirit line behind her: Queen Sunduk nearest, newly dead, then King Jinpyung, then older kings. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = jinduk, SECOND face = sunduk (an ancestral spirit in the frame), THIRD face = jinpyung (an ancestral spirit in the frame). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_moon_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels), binyeo board jinduk (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), binyeo board sunduk (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). QUEEN JINDUK — Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #9d7bd0. QUEEN SUNDUK — Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #E8552B. KING JINPYUNG Colour #5a86d6. PLACE Moon Palace (월궁) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
